help.title: Help
help.intro: LogCarve shows deterministic analytics over one configured access-log source. This page explains the filters, labels and limits you will meet on every data view.
help.filters_body: Every data view shares one filter bar: site, source, time range, display timezone, traffic and bot selectors, method, status, country and text search. Applying a new window always restarts at the first result page; switching pages keeps the full filter set. A traffic quick view replaces the traffic, bot, category, provider and purpose selectors together, a status quick view replaces status and status class together, and Largest responses only presets the Requests sort; each keeps the site, source, window and all other matchers and resets paging. Contradictory combinations are rejected instead of silently widened.
help.offsets_body: Requests are stored and filtered in UTC. The timezone selector only changes the display. Each zone option shows its signed UTC offset for the applied window start; daylight saving may shift offsets inside longer windows. Links and exports always carry full UTC instants.
help.labels_body: Bot names come from a versioned claim catalog; the dropdown shows plain names while rule IDs, versions and meanings stay exact in the API and detail panels. Categories read as AI crawlers, Search crawlers, SEO tools or Automation tools, and an empty provider or purpose reads as Unspecified. Browser-like rows are potential user traffic only: access logs alone cannot prove people, sessions, indexing, training use or conversions.
help.identity_body: Bot names are identified from User-Agent; identity not verified. True verification needs the original client address plus reverse and forward DNS checks (or approved published range matching), and original addresses are intentionally discarded, so LogCarve never proves a bot is fake or genuine. See the optional Google verification reference for what real verification requires; it is documentation only and LogCarve performs no automatic network checks.
help.privacy_body: Client addresses are HMAC-pseudonymized and original IPs never leave the import host. Query values are discarded, Referer data is minimized and secrets in paths are masked. Raw log lines and original IPs never appear in exports, error messages, API responses or assistant evidence. Country is a coarse offline estimate stored as an ISO code with lookup provenance, never an original address.
help.explorer_body: The Requests explorer lists sanitized rows in any allowlisted server sort (newest/oldest time, client, method, path, status, bytes ascending/descending) with stable timestamp/id tie-breaks and server pagination. Each row expands to a details panel with the 200-character User-Agent sample, referrer host, traffic and bot metadata, full client pseudonym, UTC and shown timestamps with offset, rule reference and the unavailable-timing note. Choosing a sort restarts at the first page; paging links advance through pages while keeping the sort direction and the full filter scope.
help.conflict_body: A conflicting-bot-identity candidate means one User-Agent carries unambiguous named bot tokens for two or more distinct providers (for example Googlebot and bingbot in one string). The known set is limited to Googlebot plus Googlebot-Image, Googlebot-News and Googlebot-Video (all Google), bingbot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, AhrefsBot, SemrushBot, MJ12bot, YandexBot and Baiduspider; underscore or hyphen affixes such as some_Googlebot_clone or my-Googlebot-tool are not counted as identity. This is a potential spoof or inconsistency lead only: identity is not verified, nothing is removed from counts, and no automatic blocking follows. True verification needs the original client address plus reverse and forward DNS checks, and original addresses are intentionally discarded, so LogCarve never proves a bot fake or genuine. The absence of this candidate also proves nothing; unknown agents stay labelled unknown or unverified.
help.troubleshooting_body: No rows usually means the selected window has no matching events: widen the range, clear the search, or check the Data Sources page for failed or partial imports. A rejected filter shows which value was invalid; nothing is silently widened. If the assistant is disabled or over budget, every deterministic table keeps working.
help.api_body: Browser pages need an admin session login. Programmatic access uses scoped API tokens with the analytics:read scope instead; tokens cannot open browser pages, import data or reach the assistant. Responses are paginated, scoped to site and time, stamped in UTC and contract-versioned.

compare.title: Compare windows
compare.baseline_note: The current window comes from the filter bar above. Pick an explicit baseline: the previous equal-length period, or a custom UTC window pair of exactly the same length with the same filters. Unequal or unparseable baselines are rejected, never widened.
compare.choose_baseline: Choose a baseline above: the previous equal-length period or an explicit UTC window pair of the same length.
compare.status_zero: Zero baseline: change is exact, ratio unavailable
compare.status_unavailable: Unavailable: empty window or limited coverage
compare.error_mismatch: Current and baseline windows must carry the same filters and span exactly equal lengths.
refresh.on_note: Auto-refresh is on; re-reading the current results.
refresh.paused_note: Auto-refresh is paused while unsaved filter changes are pending. Apply the filters to resume.
refresh.note: Re-reads the current filtered results only. Never imports, never contacts the assistant or outside services, and pauses while the tab is hidden or you are editing.
help.formats_body: LogCarve imports NCSA Combined access logs from Nginx and Apache, including gzip-compressed files and measured request-timing fields where the server records them. Import and reprocessing run only from the server command line over administratively configured source paths; the browser never uploads or picks files, so there is no import button, drag target or file chooser anywhere in this interface. The Data Sources page documents which files were imported, their status and how to reprocess them from the command line after a format change.
help.timing_body: Measured request and upstream timings arrive only when the log format records them; the units and field requirements are documented on the Data Sources and Performance pages. Missing timing is always shown as unavailable, never as zero latency, and percentiles never treat an absent value as a fast one. Cache statuses are observed log values: a 304 answer means the stored object was not sent again, not proof that a cache served it. Hit ratios divide only cache-labelled answers and stay unavailable when none exist.
help.bots_seo: Bots, SEO absence and referrer privacy
help.bots_seo_body: Bot names are claims read from User-Agent text, never verified identities. Redirect, client-error and server-error groups explain where crawlers went; empty groups mean no matching stored requests in the window, never proof of indexing, ranking or training use. AI-only paths compare against the observed universe of the same window with an explicit caveat. Referrer panels show sanitized full paths for local diagnosis, but query values are discarded, secrets in paths are masked, and only the host travels to the assistant.
help.journeys_help_body: Journeys group stored requests by client pseudonym and sanitized User-Agent with a 30-minute inactivity split: they are technical groupings, never visitors, people, browser sessions or clicks. Entry paths are each journey base-scope first request, so filters cannot move entries. Window-edge journeys are flagged partial rather than resolved by reading outside the authorized window. Times render in the selected display timezone with an explicit offset; durations keep microsecond precision so a microsecond journey never reads as zero.
help.security_cards: Security findings, 401 honesty and UTC minutes
help.security_cards_body: Security rules flag investigation candidates with exact counts and bounded samples, never confirmed attacks. Status 401 is an authentication challenge, never evidence of a failed login by a person. Tempo cards show a window average plus the peak whole UTC minute over the same rule-matching scope; a partial edge bucket is a lower-bound count over its exact interval, shown with explicit UTC endpoints.
help.ip_modes: Original address display, key separation and exact search
help.ip_modes_body: Local administrators may view original client addresses from the encrypted private store in full, suffix-masked or pseudonym-only modes; masking is display masking only. The encryption key lives apart from the database: without the valid key, or for records imported before enrichment, the display shows unavailable with reprocessing guidance instead of ciphertext. Exact-address search is a session form that translates the entry to the stable pseudonym server-side; the original is never stored in addresses, history or bookmarks, and legacy equivalent spellings keep separate identities.
help.exports_body: CSV and JSON downloads stream the complete current filtered result, not just the visible page, and always carry pseudonyms regardless of the address display mode. Every export preserves the scope, filters, window, timezone and sort metadata in its header or envelope. Oversized scopes are rejected with guidance instead of truncated; query values, raw lines and original addresses never appear in exports.
help.views_compare_body: Saved views bookmark a dashboard page with its validated filters for one admin user; creating, renaming, re-pointing and deleting all require the session check. Comparison reads the current filter window against an explicit baseline of exactly equal length and identical selectors, reporting exact changes with honest zero-baseline and empty-window notes instead of confident ratios. Auto-refresh is off by default and only re-reads the current results on a fixed interval; it never imports, never contacts the assistant, and pauses while the tab is hidden or you are editing.
help.api_n8n_body: The authenticated read-only API serves the same deterministic analytics as the dashboard, with chat disabled, no model key and no Internet. The curl and Python examples on this page use placeholder credentials; replace the host, site and UTC window, and keep real tokens out of shared notes. Automation tools such as n8n can poll the JSON endpoints with a scoped analytics:read token and the same explicit from/to UTC parameters; imports, chat and browser sessions stay separate operations with their own authorization.
help.geoip_body: Country comes from a genuine offline lookup of the eligible public client address against a locally mounted database file (DB-IP Country Lite, CC BY 4.0, credited wherever countries appear): no network request and no paid service. A country is never derived from an HMAC pseudonym, a private, reserved, loopback or documentation-range address, visitor identity or residence, or proven bot origin. Only a safe ISO country code plus the lookup source, release and status is stored. Private, reserved, loopback, documentation and invalid addresses always read as Unknown, even if a database returns a value for them. A client-address country estimate computed locally describes where an observed address is registered, never visitor identity, residence or proof of bot origin. A selection whose rows were stored without a readable database, or whose lookups yielded no country, honestly shows Unknown while ordinary analytics keep working.
help.follow_body: Incremental follow of growing log files is an explicit opt-in command-line operation (logcarve-import follow) with durable checkpoints, generation identity and rotation handling; rotated archives replay under their sealed generation (logcarve-import replay-archive). The dashboard only ever shows already imported data, and the optional refresh only re-reads imports. Nothing in the browser starts, watches or tails a file, and no live watcher or system service is installed by this task.
